quote.text: The beginning is the most important part of the work.
quote.author: Plato, Republic, Book II (c. 375 BC)

stories.headline: Two Working Groups, and the Word Neither Side Will Say First
stories.dek: Jared Kushner ran a Cairo-to-Jerusalem shuttle to rescue a stalled Gaza roadmap. He came away with committees, optimism, and no answer to the only question that matters: who moves first.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 3 · Chinese Woks
stories.headline: Buy the Cheap One, Burn It Blue, Keep It Forever
stories.dek: The most-used pan in a Singapore kitchen, taken to its makers. The physics is in the metal and the gauge; the non-stick is a patina you build yourself; and the grail tier mostly buys a better story.

stories.headline: The Machine That Never Dies, and the Number That Never Stops
stories.dek: Indoor rowing is the rare hobby where the entry-level purchase is also the endgame purchase — a Concept2 you buy once and race against for the rest of your life. The hook is a single figure on a small grey screen.

stories.headline: The Growth Chart Is Vertical. The Rally Is About the Power Bill.
stories.dek: The Prime Minister gives Sunday's National Day Rally — his third. The economy just got an upgrade, but the speech will be judged on the tariff that landed in July, not the GDP print that followed.

stories.headline: The Strongest Open Coder Shipped — and Held Its Weights
stories.dek: Z.ai put GLM-5.3's coding API live this week and called it the best open-weights coder going. Then it kept the weights back for a fortnight of safety testing. Ship the product first, release the thing everyone actually wants second — a deliberate order, and a telling one.

stories.headline: Thinner, Stronger, Nineteen Hundred Dollars — and a Smaller Battery
stories.dek: Google's Pixel 11 Pro Fold ships Thursday. The build got better in every direction but one, and the one is the cell inside it.

stories.headline: A Farewell in Orange, Charged by Daylight
stories.dek: TAG Heuer sends off the final Dutch Grand Prix with a solar-quartz Formula 1 in Zandvoort orange. Charming, practical, well-priced — and a "limited" run the grey market has already outrun.

stories.headline: The Record the Critics Adore, and the One You'll Actually Replay
stories.dek: L'Rain's "fata morgana" is the best-reviewed album of the season — a collage of dancehall, gospel and crunched metal. Whether it lives on your headphones or just in the reviews is the honest question.

stories.headline: The Phone-Ban Payoff Arrives in Year Three
stories.dek: The largest study yet of school phone bans finds a real gain in student well-being — larger than switching off Facebook — but only after the friction of year one, and next to nothing on grades. The order is the finding.

stories.headline: The Long End Did the Fed's Job First
stories.dek: The thirty-year went to a nineteen-year high while the front end priced cuts. That is a bear steepener — and it says the market's worry has moved from the central bank to the government that funds it.

stories.headline: The Barbell Comes First; the Protein Only Permits It
stories.dek: The 2026 evidence has moved from how much to lift to what to eat around it — and a clean null trial just put the popular shortcut in its place. The muscle is built by the training; the powder is raw material, not a lever.

stories.headline: October Is Already Full — Book It Before Someone Else Does
The Country That Went Furthest Into the Feed Is Quietly Backing Out
stories.dek: The Philippines was the test market for the real-name, algorithmic web — and the cautionary tale of what it did to trust. Now, at the exact moment that trust is collapsing faster than anywhere on earth, young Filipinos are slipping toward the opposite kind of platform: anonymous, text-first, community-run. They are rebuilding the public square the last one poisoned.
